study_id: Kampaktsis et al. - 2023 - Machine learning-based prediction of mortality after heart transplantation in adults with congenital

eligibility.Eligibility Rationale: The study analyzes adult heart transplant recipients using a CatBoost machine learning model to predict post‑transplant mortality, meeting all population, AI, outcome, and publication criteria.

identification_methods.Comments: Retrospective analysis of UNOS database focusing on adult congenital heart disease patients undergoing heart transplantation.
identification_methods.Address: 177 Fort Washington Avenue, MHB2, New York, NY 10032, USA
identification_methods.Dataset Source: United Network for Organ Sharing (UNOS) database
identification_methods.Identification Notes: Included adult ACHD patients who underwent isolated heart transplantation; excluded non‑adults, prior transplants, multi‑organ transplants, and those with <1 year follow‑up; variables with >10% missing values were not analyzed.
identification_methods.Class Imbalance: Random oversampling applied to balance outcome classes in training set
identification_methods.Input Variables: Recipient, donor, procedural and post‑transplant characteristics (49 variables initially, 10 selected via SHAP)
identification_methods.Missing Data Handling: Variables with >10% missing values excluded; no imputation performed
identification_methods.Validation Method: Random split into derivation (70%) and validation (30%) cohorts; internal validation on held‑out set
identification_methods.Methods Notes: Feature selection using SHAP; oversampling for class imbalance; performance assessed with AUC, accuracy, sensitivity, specificity; SHAP used for explainability and individual risk assessment

population.Inclusion criteria: Adult ACHD patients who underwent isolated heart transplantation in the UNOS database from 2000 to 2020
population.Exclusion criteria: Non-adult patients, prior transplantation, simultaneous heart and other organ transplants, less than 1-year follow-up
population.Target Population: Adult congenital heart disease heart transplant recipients
population.Population Notes: Cohort randomly split into derivation (70%) and validation (30%) datasets

interventions_outcomes.Intervention Input Data Modality: UNOS registry tabular clinical variables (recipient, donor, procedural, post-transplant characteristics)
interventions_outcomes.Feature Selection Method: SHAP (recursive feature elimination using SHapley Additive exPlanations)
interventions_outcomes.Temporal Handling: Static baseline and early post-transplant data
interventions_outcomes.Interventions Notes: Random split 70% training / 30% validation, random oversampling of minority class, CatBoost model trained on selected variables
interventions_outcomes.Outcomes Notes: Mortality after heart transplantation in adults with congenital heart disease
interventions_outcomes.Result data Notes: AUC .80 for 1-year model, .69 for 3-year model; predictive accuracies 75.2% and 74.2% respectively
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome group: All adult ACHD heart transplant recipients (n=1033) in validation cohort
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome Metric Definition: Area under the receiver operating characteristic curve on validation cohort
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome Notes: Satisfactory predictive accuracy of mortality prediction
